topic: Eigenvalues, Eigenvectors, and the Power Iteration

entry_point.discipline_context: Use modal reasoning and matrix-based engineering computation as bounded framing for directions and transformations.
entry_point.rationale: The learner knows vectors, matrices, calculus, and basic NumPy but not iterative eigensolvers.
entry_point.analogy_boundary: The engineering framing is a learning analogy and does not assert an unsupported physical interpretation.

conditional_item_decisions.rationale: The scope requires the characteristic equation.
The scope requires the non-symmetric limitation.
The scope requires NumPy implementation semantics.
The scope requires positive-integer max_iterations validation and corrected implementation semantics.
The scope requires the worked matrix result.

chapter_sequence.title: Eigenpairs and the characteristic equation
chapter_sequence.purpose: Build definitions and connect exact eigenvalue equations to the iterative setting.

chapter_sequence.title: Dominant modes in symmetric matrices
chapter_sequence.purpose: Explain the symmetric spectral decomposition and magnitude dominance.

chapter_sequence.title: Deriving power iteration and its convergence
chapter_sequence.purpose: Derive normalized iteration and state its assumptions and asymptotic rate.

chapter_sequence.title: Estimates, residuals, and algorithm behaviour
chapter_sequence.purpose: Use the Rayleigh quotient and residual and organize algorithm checks.

chapter_sequence.title: Failure cases and a NumPy implementation
chapter_sequence.purpose: Diagnose failure cases, scope limits, and implement the validated algorithm.

chapter_sequence.title: Exercises and worked solutions
chapter_sequence.purpose: Consolidate concepts, one power-iteration calculation, and implementation diagnosis.

implementation_strategy: Present the normalized matrix-vector iteration, input validation, breakdown check, residual stopping test, positive iteration limit, and four-value return structure in executable NumPy code.
assessment_strategy: Use exactly one concept check, one unified power-iteration hand calculation, and one code diagnostic in a final chapter after all instruction.

exercise_plan.learning_objective: Explain magnitude dominance and sign ambiguity.
exercise_plan.discipline_context: Interpret an estimated modal direction without assigning significance to its arbitrary sign.

exercise_plan.learning_objective: Compute one power-iteration step, Rayleigh quotient, residual, and residual norm.
exercise_plan.discipline_context: Trace one small matrix calculation as a model of matrix-based engineering computation.

exercise_plan.learning_objective: Locate and correct missing positive-integer max_iterations validation.
exercise_plan.discipline_context: Diagnose a numerical implementation before using it in an engineering computation.
